svg.text: TOKEIRA · ARCHITECTURE
The two wire worlds
One crate, two protobuf surfaces with different constitutions: Temporal's contract, preserved exactly — and Tokeira's own, versioned on its own terms.
THE COMPATIBILITY WORLD — TEMPORAL'S WIRE
Vendored, versioned, never extended
proto/upstream/ — Temporal API v1.62.11 · tonic + prost
WorkflowService, OperatorService, and every message SDKs already speak,
compiled exactly as Temporal published them. The behavioural contract is
pinned to server v1.31.0 and verified by the conformance corpus.
The constitution: fidelity
No Tokeira extension fields, ever — compatibility metadata that needs the wire
gets its own packages instead of touching upstream messages.
Who speaks it
Every SDK and worker, over gRPC · the HTTP/JSON gateway, transcoding the same
descriptors · the functional conformance harness, over the real wire.
changes arrive only by vendoring a new upstream version — a reviewed, pinned event
THE FIRST-PARTY WORLD — TOKEIRA'S WIRE
Owned, Connect-spoken, public in its own right
proto/tokeira/ — buffa codegen + connect-rust · the Connect protocol
Tokeira's own interface: fleet coordination (membership, routing, drain),
the conformance control service, and operator-facing compatibility metadata
— tkr already speaks it. This is where Tokeira-native capability lands.
The constitution: ownership
The contract is Tokeira's to version — v1 packages under proto/tokeira/,
evolved deliberately, at Tokeira's pace.
Standing on governed ground
connect-rust — Anthropic-built, now under official Connect governance — passes
the complete Connect conformance suite. A dependency validated like tokeira is.
legacy corner, stated honestly: some internal runtime/admin packages still ride tonic/prost
tokeira-proto — one crate, both worlds
modules: public · internal · connect · conversions
Bindings are generated ahead of time and checked in — building needs neither protoc nor the
proto tree. cargo run -p proto-sync -- generate regenerates both worlds in one deterministic pass.
Why the split exists
The compatibility world holds still by design: Temporal's surface changes only when the pins move, so "your SDKs already speak this" stays checkable.
The first-party world is Tokeira's own product surface — it evolves at Tokeira's pace and is where the platform grows beyond compatibility. One crate
holds both so a single conversion layer — not scattered glue — is the only place the worlds meet.
Companions: the compatibility edge (where the public world is served) · two authorities (the internal world's biggest speaker) · docs/crates/proto.md.
